body: Scion Capital (Nov 2000-2008): +489.34% net of fees to June 2008 vs ~2-3% for the S&P 500 incl. dividends; investors made ~$700m+, Burry ~$100m. Early gains came from deep value and shorting dot-com stocks (2001 +55% per a blog, less reliable). Signature trade: from May 2005 bought credit default swaps on subprime mortgage bonds (first $60m from Deutsche Bank) after reading the actual loan pools in prospectuses; investors revolted and he side-pocketed positions during 2006-07 losses before the payoff; he exited CDS by April 2008. Structural edge: a tiny, unconstrained fund able to buy obscure securities; process edge: reads primary documents others skip, EV/EBITDA-style deep value screens, willingness to look wrong for 2+ years. Later: GameStop stake 2019 (sold before most of the 2021 squeeze); public 'crash' warnings repeatedly early (e.g., 2023 'Sell' tweet and index puts); deregistered Scion Asset Management in Nov 2025 after bearish AI-hyperscaler depreciation calls. Mistakes: investor-relations failure in 2006-07; serial premature macro calls. Copyable: read the annual report, notes and loan/collateral disclosures yourself; size contrarian bets so you can survive being early. Do not copy: public doom predictions as a timing tool.
